page: Microsoft Azure F8-2ams_v7 is an x86_64 virtual machine instance powered by an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor clocked at 4.5 GHz. The server is configured with 2 dedicated vCPUs corresponding to 2 physical cores (1 thread per core) paired with 64.0 GB of system memory, delivering a high memory-to-core ratio of 32.0 GB per vCPU. The hardware architecture includes 48 KB of L1d cache, 1.0 MB of L2 cache, and 32 MB of L3 cache per core cluster, with CPU instruction extensions including AVX-512 (F, VNNI, BF16), SHA-NI, and VAES. There are no attached GPUs or bundled local storage devices included with this instance, requiring external network-attached volumes for persistent data.

Benchmark results demonstrate strong single-thread performance, ranking in the top tier for stress-ng single-core execution (3600.69) and Geekbench single-core testing (2865.0). Memory and compression tests also reflect high single-threaded throughput, registering 38.86 GB/sec in single-threaded gzip compression and 17.39 GB/sec in single-threaded bzip3 decompression. However, because the instance provides only 2 physical cores, aggregate multi-threaded capacity is constrained. Multi-core stress-ng (7221.66) and Geekbench multi-core (5149.0) scores settle in the average range, while multi-threaded bzip3 decompression and PassMark total CPU performance fall into the bottom tier.

With its 32:1 memory-to-core ratio, the F8-2ams_v7 functions effectively as a memory-optimized host for tasks needing large RAM capacities but relatively few execution threads. It achieves 6.96 million operations per second in Redis SET operations and steady throughput in database operation benchmarks. Conversely, compute-intensive multi-threaded tasks such as software compilation, ray tracing, and hosting larger 7B language models exhibit limited performance due to core count constraints. It is best suited for in-memory caching layers, medium-scale relational or NoSQL databases, memory-intensive data preprocessing, and applications prioritizing single-thread clock speed over parallel scaling.
description: Microsoft Azure F8-2ams_v7 is a compute-designated, memory-intensive virtual machine featuring 2 dedicated x86_64 vCPUs on an AMD EPYC 9V45 processor running at 4.5 GHz, coupled with 64.0 GB of RAM. The instance lacks bundled local storage and GPU accelerators, relying on remote storage architectures. Due to its dedicated 4.5 GHz cores and modern instruction sets including AVX-512, the system demonstrates top-tier single-core benchmark performance, including high single-threaded compression and Geekbench single-core metrics. Its 32.0 GB per core memory footprint allows large working sets, though aggregate multi-threaded execution is naturally capped by the 2-core allotment. Benchmark tests show average Redis SET performance (6.96 million ops/sec) and database operation throughput, offset by lower performance in heavy parallel tasks like software compilation and LLM inference. The F8-2ams_v7 is suitable for in-memory databases, caching engines, and memory-heavy workloads with limited concurrency.
